judged_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:344-355 — [P1; confidence 100] `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true } } }, where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` loads any credential by attacker-controlled destinationCalendar.credentialId without user/team ownership scope and then passes its key to `createEvent`, so a crafted booking can write events through another tenant's OAuth token; the strongest rebuttal—that the ID came from a persisted destination calendar—is insufficient because the new fallback explicitly trusts the ID and the query itself enforces no relationship to the current EventManager credentials or organizer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in EventManager.ts lines 344-370, when a credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the code fetches it directly from the database using `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` without any ownership verification. The `destination.credentialId` comes from `event.destinationCalendar` which is passed into the EventManager. While destinationCalendar typically comes from database records, the new fallback code explicitly trusts this ID and queries any credential in the system without checking if it belongs to the current user/team. This could allow accessing another tenant's OAuth credentials if an attacker can control the destinationCalendar.credentialId value. The same pattern appears in the updateAllCalendarEvents method around lines 510-530.
